title: Load balancer pulls an unready replica from rotation via the readiness probe without triggering a restart
asA: load balancer or service mesh routing traffic across replicas of the deployed application
iWant: a readiness endpoint that answers pass or fail based on whether the process can serve request traffic against its declared dependencies
soThat: I stop routing traffic to a replica that has lost a required dependency without the orchestrator restarting a process that would come back to the same failure

acceptanceCriteria.description: The application serves the readiness endpoint at a stable HTTP path declared in configuration (default /readyz), distinct from the liveness path; a GET returns 200 with a JSON body when every declared readiness dependency is passing and returns 503 with a JSON body when at least one declared readiness dependency is failing.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running and the readiness dependency set is declared
acceptanceCriteria.when: an unauthenticated GET is issued against the readiness path against a healthy dependency set, then against a set with at least one failing dependency
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first response has status code 200 with JSON body status equal to pass; the second response has status code 503 with JSON body status equal to fail; both bodies have Content-Type application/json

acceptanceCriteria.description: The readiness path is served on the same HTTP listener as the application's request traffic (not on a separate operator port), so a load balancer probing readiness observes the same reachability the traffic will observe.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running and the request-traffic listener address is declared
acceptanceCriteria.when: a GET is issued against the readiness path targeting the same listener address as request traffic
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is served by the application, not refused with a connection error, and the readiness handler and a representative request handler both bind to the same address:port pair as reported by the process

acceptanceCriteria.description: A readiness probe fail never triggers a process exit: the process remains up and continues answering liveness with pass while readiness answers fail.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running with at least one declared readiness dependency in a failed state
acceptanceCriteria.when: the readiness probe returns 503 across a five-minute window
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process exit code is not emitted, the process remains running throughout the window, and the liveness probe continues to return 200 with status pass
